filename: Simulating the Air Quality Impact of Prescribed Fires Using Graph Neural Network-Based PM2.5 Forecasts.pdf
title: Simulating the Air Quality Impact of Prescribed Fires Using Graph Neural Network-Based PM2.5 Forecasts
testbed_rationale: The paper focuses on forecasting point-sensor air quality concentrations using graph neural networks rather than parameterizing unresolved subgrid physical processes within numerical weather or climate models.
pain_points: Ground monitors are spatially sparse and have missing observation records requiring imputation
Model tends to output values close to the previous timestep (persistence bias)
Lack of ground-truth observations to independently evaluate partitioned fire-specific vs. ambient PM2.5 concentrations
Difficulty identifying and filtering time steps fully uninfluenced by persistent smoke (fire influence persists up to 10 days)
extraction_notes: The research was funded in part by NSF LEAP STC (Award #2019625). Prescribed burns were simulated by transposing historical prescribed fire FRP to counterfactual target times within the GNN.
